question: I'm a senior psych major applying to clinical psych PhD programs. which psych profs at ramapo do research in clinical or developmental psych, and do any of them take undergrads as research assistants?

body.answer:
The college catalog lists 12 people as faculty of Psychology (Psychology BA, Psychology Minor) [17][18]:
- Naseem Choudhury, program convener, Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience, nchoudhu@ramapo.edu [19]
- Joseph F. Cataliotti, Associate Professor of Neuropsychology, jcatalio@ramapo.edu [20]
- Sandra Gonsalves-Domond, Professor of Psychology, vdomond@ramapo.edu [21]
- Shaziela Ishak, Professor of Psychology, sishak@ramapo.edu [22]
- Kathleen Lynch, Associate Professor of Neuroscience, klynch13@ramapo.edu [23]
- James Morley, Professor of Clinical Psychology, jmorley@ramapo.edu [24]
- Lysandra Perez-Strumolo, Associate Professor of Psychology, lperezst@ramapo.edu [25]
- Maya Poran, Professor of Psychology, mporan@ramapo.edu [26]
- Christian Reich, Professor of Psychology (Behavioral Neuroscience), creich@ramapo.edu [27]
- Tilahun Sineshaw, Professor of Psychology, tsinesha@ramapo.edu [28]
- Jessica Terrizzi, Assistant Professor of Clinical Psychology, jterriz1@ramapo.edu [29]
- Leah Warner, Professor of Psychology, lwarner@ramapo.edu [30]

I don’t have verified information identifying which psychology professors research clinical or developmental psychology. The Office of the Provost’s page says Ramapo supports opportunities for students to work alongside faculty in research [14]; it does not say which professors take undergraduates as research assistants. The School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office may be able to help identify faculty to ask.

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [41]

Sources: [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/research-and-scholarship/) [17](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [18](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MN-PSYC) [19](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/naseem-choudhury/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/joseph-f-cataliotti/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/sandra-gonsalves-domond/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/shaziela-ishak/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/kathleen-lynch/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/james-morley/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/lysandra-perez-strumolo/) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/maya-poran/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/christian-reich/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/tilahun-sineshaw/) [29](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/jessica-terrizzi/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/leah-warner/) [41](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: office of specialized services hrs? need to set up testing accomodations b4 finals and idk who to email there

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

OSS office hours are typically Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM–4:30 PM. Meetings are by appointment; schedule with your OSS Advisor through Connect at web.ramapo.edu. [6]

For testing accommodations, submit exam requests through OSSOnline. The student testing agreement says to reserve no later than 14 days before final exams. [1,7] Email osstests@ramapo.edu about alternative testing. [3]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [27]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/alternative-testing-for-faculty/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/oss-staff-contact-information/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/alternative-testing-for-students/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: im undecided n have no clue what to major in lol who do i talk to for advising n wheres their office at

body.answer:
Since you’re undecided, contact the Center for Student Success; their advisors help students who haven’t declared a major through the Ramapo Exploration Program. [1] Their office is D-207. [2]

For a virtual or in-person walk-in, sign in through the Virtual Kiosk on Connect; you need an activated Ramapo email address. In-person check-in is at the kiosk in the D207 main office. [8]

**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [28]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/home/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is there a list of ramapos senior leadership somewhere like all the vps n what each one is in charge of

body.answer:
Yes. The Office of the President page lists the Senior Leadership: Mission Element Team: [https://www.ramapo.edu/president/](https://www.ramapo.edu/president/) [1]

- Michael Middleton — Provost | Vice President for Teaching, Learning, and Growth
- Virginia Galdieri — Vice President for People Operations & Employee Resources
- Patrick W. O’Connor — Vice President for Government Relations & Business Development
- Colleen O’Keefe — Chief Financial Officer | Vice President for Fiscal Health
- Nicole Morgan-Agard — Vice President | General Counsel
- Christopher Romano — Vice President for Strategic Enrollment, Outreach & Engagement | Executive Director of the RCNJ Foundation
- Melissa Van Der Wall — Dean of Students | Vice President for Student Well-being
- Brittany A. Williams-Goldstein — Chief of Staff & Board Liaison | Vice President for Policy, Research & Governance | College Spokesperson
- Michael Yankovich — Vice President for Operational & Administrative Integration [1]

The College Organizational Chart is also linked from the Board of Trustees resources page; it is routinely updated by the People Operations and Employee Resources Department and in most cases presents three tiers of leadership. In-depth multi-tiered organizational charts of individual units are available upon request: [https://www.ramapo.edu/college-leadership/](https://www.ramapo.edu/college-leadership/) [15]

- **Office of the President**: Phone: (201) 684-7607. [27]
- **Board of Trustees**: Email: trustee@ramapo.edu. [27]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/president/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/board/trustee-resources/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

body.answer:
The Library offers in-person help during Research Help Desk hours and virtual help; its page lists the times [6]. You can make a research appointment: [https://libcal.ramapo.edu/appointments](https://libcal.ramapo.edu/appointments) [4]. To email reference librarians, use [https://www.ramapo.edu/library/email-reference-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/email-reference-form/); the service is for Ramapo students, faculty and staff, and you should get a response within 24 hours except weekends and holidays [11]. For an immediate response, go to the library website, click the “Ask a Librarian” icon, then type your question in the chat box; you’ll get an immediate response if they are online [11]. If chat is offline, email refdesk@ramapo.edu [4, 9]. Christina Connor is listed as Assessment and Instruction Librarian, with a liaison assignment to ASB and American History Textbook Project Coordinator; the page does not identify a communication or media studies liaison [10].

**Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [16]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/research-help-services/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/library-news/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/research-help-services/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/staff-directory/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/email-reference-form/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: which psych prof writes the best rec letters for grad school?? need 3 strong ones n ngl idk who to ask

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

The college catalog lists 12 people as faculty of Psychology (Psychology BA, Psychology Minor) [15][16]:
- Naseem Choudhury, program convener, Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience, nchoudhu@ramapo.edu [17]
- Joseph F. Cataliotti, Associate Professor of Neuropsychology, jcatalio@ramapo.edu [18]
- Sandra Gonsalves-Domond, Professor of Psychology, vdomond@ramapo.edu [19]
- Shaziela Ishak, Professor of Psychology, sishak@ramapo.edu [20]
- Kathleen Lynch, Associate Professor of Neuroscience, klynch13@ramapo.edu [21]
- James Morley, Professor of Clinical Psychology, jmorley@ramapo.edu [22]
- Lysandra Perez-Strumolo, Associate Professor of Psychology, lperezst@ramapo.edu [23]
- Maya Poran, Professor of Psychology, mporan@ramapo.edu [24]
- Christian Reich, Professor of Psychology (Behavioral Neuroscience), creich@ramapo.edu [25]
- Tilahun Sineshaw, Professor of Psychology, tsinesha@ramapo.edu [26]
- Jessica Terrizzi, Assistant Professor of Clinical Psychology, jterriz1@ramapo.edu [27]
- Leah Warner, Professor of Psychology, lwarner@ramapo.edu [28]

I don’t find published information identifying which psychology professors write graduate-school recommendation letters. The Prestigious Fellowships and Scholarships office offers individual counseling, including graduate-school guidance, help obtaining effective letters of recommendation, and faculty advice. Complete its questionnaire to get help matched with opportunities [31]. It also recommends approaching recommenders months in advance, discussing your plans and reasons for applying, and providing a written program description, essay, transcript (if requested), and honors list [4]. Its advice for writers says strong letters give specific details about your work, strengths, and the writer’s relationship with you [3].

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/prestigious-fellowships-and-scholarships/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/prestigious-fellowships-and-scholarships/) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [16](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MN-PSYC) [17](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/naseem-choudhury/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/joseph-f-cataliotti/) [19](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/sandra-gonsalves-domond/) [20](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/shaziela-ishak/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/kathleen-lynch/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/james-morley/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/lysandra-perez-strumolo/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/maya-poran/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/christian-reich/) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/tilahun-sineshaw/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/jessica-terrizzi/) [28](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/faculty/leah-warner/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/prestigious-fellowships-and-scholarships/)

body.answer:
That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

The calendar lists no event this weekend, Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22 that matches what you asked [1].

All 10 events this weekend, Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22:

Friday, November 20:
- 6:30 PM to 7:30 PM: WingsGiving (The Village), at Village Thomases Commons [2]
- 7:30 PM to 10 PM: RCNJ Theater Presents: As You Like It (CA Theater Program Productions), at Sharp Theater [3]
- 9 PM to 11 PM: Build Your Own Self Care Basket (College Programming Board) [4]

Saturday, November 21:
- 3 PM to 5 PM: Men's Basketball vs. Farmingdale State College (\#WeAreRCNJ), at Bradley Center Arena [5]
- 7:30 PM to 10 PM: RCNJ Theater Presents: As You Like It (CA Theater Program Productions), at Sharp Theater [6]
- 9 PM to 11 PM: Cozy Night (College Programming Board) [7]

Sunday, November 22:
- 10 AM to 2 PM: RCNJ Shuttle Highlight: Ramsey Farmers Market (Civic and Community Engagement Center), at Bradley Center Bus Stop [8]
- 11:30 AM to 3:30 PM: Spanish Club Museum Trip (Spanish Club) [9]
- 2 PM to 3 PM: Friendsgiving Pie & Gratitude Lounge (The Village), at Thomases Commons [10]
- 8 PM to 9 PM: Blind Box Bingo (The Overlook), at Overlook 1st Floor Lounge [11]

Residence Life says events are for all Ramapo students, and you can subscribe to its calendar and set alerts or check event dates and times on Archway [15]. For ideas, talk to your RA [13].

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [24]

These offices can help:
- **Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [25]
- **Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [25]

question: Hi, I'm an international student from Vietnam. is there an international student club or cultural association where i can meet other students from Asia?

body.answer:
Hi! That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

Yes. The International Student Organization welcomes students of all nationalities. It meets regularly and plans activities and events, including international dinner nights, films, lectures, off-campus trips, International Student Week, and the International Food Festival. [1][23]

The United Asian Association focuses on Asian-Pacific Islander American cultures and diversity, and promotes understanding of APIA culture, history, and politics. [2][24]

You can also explore the South Asian Club, which holds events highlighting South Asian culture, music, art, and traditions. [25]

The club directory lists the International Student Organization: [https://archway.ramapo.edu/ISO/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/ISO/) [1]; United Asian Association: [https://archway.ramapo.edu/UAA/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/UAA/) [2]; and South Asian Club: [https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAC/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAC/) [36].

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [47]

This office can help:
**Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [48]

Sources: [1](https://archway.ramapo.edu/ISO/) [2](https://archway.ramapo.edu/UAA/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/international-student-organization-iso/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/united-asian-association-uaa/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/south-asians-ramapo/) [36](https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAC/) [47](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [48](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Having had visited most of Europe by the end of high school, I knew I wanted to go farther out for my college education. This was when I decided to study in the United States—a bold decision, which few of my peers at the time would understand or agree with. In fact, although most of my friends and family were extremely happy and proud of me for my decision, most wondered why I would choose to go so far. The answer was that navigating and exploring a different “world” can be extremely rewarding. Indeed, over the four years I spent at Ramapo I received a world-class education, achieved high academic success, gained experience at one of the most thriving companies in the fashion industry, made many supportive and kind-hearted friends, and learned to be more flexible, independent, and mature. Conversely, I now clearly recognize that a country which fosters diversity and welcomes international students experiences both social and economic benefits for the larger community. Lastly, I am extremely grateful for the kind, supportive, and highly responsive team of Roukema Center (https://www.ramapo.edu/international/). Thank you, Raj, Izumi, and Ben for always being there for us! -Victor Georgiev, Ramapo College Class of 2019 I came to the United States 13 years ago as an international student. The process wasn’t easy – it involved a lot of sacrifice, hard work, and tears. Despite the challenges, I was committed to pursue it because it was my dream. I knew there was no other country in the world that would provide me the same opportunities, liberties, and freedom. Studying at Ramapo College gave me all of this – opportunity to study what I liked, liberty to express my views, freedom to believe that everything is possible as long as I worked hard for it and pursued it with passion and commitment. I believe that international students do enrich and add value to the community in a tangible way – help with tutoring or on-campus work- but more importantly intangible – with knowledge, diverse perspectives, different and innovative thinking, exchange of culture, language, food, love.. I think it is hard to put a price tag on these attributes. If you extrapolate this on a country level, I think the same could be said. One can measure the economic activity of international students (which overtime is not marginal), but for many of us this would be the least of the important services we provide to this country which while may not be our “native” country, its our home country – and we love it and care about it. -Dorina Georgieva, Ramapo College Class of 2011 Studying in the United States as international student was the biggest challenge and the greatest achievement of my life. Each embassy or consular post has their own visa application procedures and processing times, but in general, to apply you will need to submit your I-20 Form (for F-1) or DS-2019 Form (for J-1), along with your passport, proof of financial support, SEVIS fee receipt, photos, visa application fee, and the appropriate visa application forms. answer:
Hi! That sounds really hard, and a lot of students feel this way, especially at first. You're not the only one.

Yes. The International Student Organization welcomes students of all nationalities. It meets regularly and plans activities and events, including international dinner nights, films, lectures, off-campus trips, International Student Week, and the International Food Festival. [1][23]

The United Asian Association focuses on Asian-Pacific Islander American cultures and diversity, and promotes understanding of APIA culture, history, and politics. [2][24]

You can also explore the South Asian Club, which holds events highlighting South Asian culture, music, art, and traditions. [25]

The club directory lists the International Student Organization: [https://archway.ramapo.edu/ISO/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/ISO/) [1]; United Asian Association: [https://archway.ramapo.edu/UAA/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/UAA/) [2]; and South Asian Club: [https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAC/](https://archway.ramapo.edu/SAC/) [36].

question: what do me n my friends gotta do to start a new club? tryna make a knitting/crochet one

body.answer:
Ramapo already lists a Knit and Crochet Club, created to bring together students seeking a creative and social outlet and to help students learn skills they can enjoy recreationally and use to make a positive impact in the community. You could contact them about joining or bringing your idea to the existing club: knitcrochet@ramapo.edu. [1]

If you want to start a different or new club, the College says to inquire with the Center for Student Involvement about starting one. [3] SGA’s Club Process & Allocations Committee works with students who want to start new clubs. The Vice President first instructs students on how to start one; then the Committee reviews the proposed constitution and Archway application. [14]

I don’t have verified information about the specific steps, eligibility requirements, or forms for proposing a new club. Contact the Center for Student Involvement or SGA’s Club Process & Allocations Committee.

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [27]

Ramapo already lists a Knit and Crochet Club, created to bring together students seeking a creative and social outlet and to help students learn skills they can enjoy recreationally and use to make a positive impact in the community. You could contact them about joining or bringing your idea to the existing club: knitcrochet@ramapo.edu. [1]

If you want to start a different or new club, the College says to inquire with the Center for Student Involvement about starting one. [3] SGA’s Club Process & Allocations Committee works with students who want to start new clubs. The Vice President first instructs students on how to start one; then the Committee reviews the proposed constitution and Archway application. [14]

I don’t have verified information about the specific steps, eligibility requirements, or forms for proposing a new club. Contact the Center for Student Involvement or SGA’s Club Process & Allocations Committee.

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [27]

question: how do i contact the photography club, wanna ask if beginners w/o a real camera can join

body.answer:
Center for Student Involvement email: csi@ramapo.edu. [1] Center for Student Involvement phone: (201) 684-7593. [1] Center for Student Involvement is in SC-202. [1] Center for Student Involvement: Comments, Questions, Concerns? Email csi@ramapo.edu or call 201-684-7593. [1]

Center for Student Involvement's page "Photography Club" says: "Photography Club’s mission is to help students on campus through creativity, collaboration, competition, and involvement. Students who join Photography Club will gain valuable social skills, career advantages, friendships, networking, and a fun environment to share photos. The Club will help students of all skill levels get into photography while also being professional to help support other clubs and organizations. Email: photographyclub@ramapo.edu (mailto:photographyclub@ramapo.edu)" [2]

Center for Student Involvement's page "Yearbook Club" says: "Calling all creative Roadrunners! The Yearbook Club is your backstage pass to making Ramapo College’s annual yearbook a masterpiece. Whether you’re snapping pics, designing layouts, crafting captions, or captaining the ship, you’ll get to flex your creative muscles while building skills like photography, graphic design, writing, editing, leadership, and teamwork. Plus, you’ll leave your mark on campus and create something your fellow Roadrunners will treasure forever. Sure, it’s a commitment—but one filled with laughs, learning, and a whole lot of pride when you hold the final product." (more on its page) [3]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/photography-club/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/yearbook-club/)

Center for Student Involvement email: csi@ramapo.edu. [1] Center for Student Involvement phone: (201) 684-7593. [1] Center for Student Involvement is in SC-202. [1] Center for Student Involvement: Comments, Questions, Concerns? Email csi@ramapo.edu or call 201-684-7593. [1]

Center for Student Involvement's page "Photography Club" says: "Photography Club’s mission is to help students on campus through creativity, collaboration, competition, and involvement. Students who join Photography Club will gain valuable social skills, career advantages, friendships, networking, and a fun environment to share photos. The Club will help students of all skill levels get into photography while also being professional to help support other clubs and organizations. Email: photographyclub@ramapo.edu (mailto:photographyclub@ramapo.edu)" [2]

Center for Student Involvement's page "Yearbook Club" says: "Calling all creative Roadrunners! The Yearbook Club is your backstage pass to making Ramapo College’s annual yearbook a masterpiece. Whether you’re snapping pics, designing layouts, crafting captions, or captaining the ship, you’ll get to flex your creative muscles while building skills like photography, graphic design, writing, editing, leadership, and teamwork. Plus, you’ll leave your mark on campus and create something your fellow Roadrunners will treasure forever. Sure, it’s a commitment—but one filled with laughs, learning, and a whole lot of pride when you hold the final product." (more on its page) [3]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/photography-club/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/organization/yearbook-club/)

question: where n when does msa meet (muslim student association)

body.answer:
Center for Student Involvement: Comments, Questions, Concerns? Email csi@ramapo.edu or call 201-684-7593. [1] Center for Student Involvement is in SC-202. [1] Center for Student Involvement hours: Monday to Friday: 8:00am-12:00am; Saturday: 4:00pm-10:00pm; Sunday: 3:00pm-8:00pm. [3] Center for Student Involvement (Summer) hours: Monday to Thursday: 8:00am-5:15pm; Friday to Sunday: not published (checked November 17, 2026). [5]

Center for Student Involvement's page "Muslim Student Association (MSA)" says: "Muslim Student Association will provide all members of the Ramapo Community with an understanding of Islam. The primary goal of the MSA will be to serve the best interests of the students of Ramapo College. The specific goals of the MSA include, but are not limited to, creating and raising awareness and understanding of Islam on campus as well as fostering a sense of community and brotherhood/sisterhood among the students. The MSA will also promote a sense of appreciation of the core Islamic teachings to both Muslims and non-Muslims through its events and activities while providing services to facilitate a comfortable, safe, and peaceful campus environment." (more on its page) (its page was last updated September 2021) [2] Center for Student Involvement has no verified hours for any day. [4]

The Multicultural Center and the Office of Access, Belonging and Community (ABC)'s page "Faith and Spirituality" says: "Ramapo’s faith-based student organizations provide opportunities to explore faith, connect with others, celebrate traditions, and build community. Whether you’re looking for a community that shares your faith or interested in learning about different religious traditions, these organizations offer ways to connect and get involved. Explore their upcoming programs and opportunities below: Muslim Student Association (MSA) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship (IVCF) Newman Catholic Hillel Chabad Interfaith Prayer & Reflection Space…" (more on its page) [6]

The page does not say which dates this schedule covers. [3][5]

I don't have verified information about that part.

Center for Student Involvement's page "Muslim Student Association (MSA)" says: "Muslim Student Association will provide all members of the Ramapo Community with an understanding of Islam. The primary goal of the MSA will be to serve the best interests of the students of Ramapo College. The specific goals of the MSA include, but are not limited to, creating and raising awareness and understanding of Islam on campus as well as fostering a sense of community and brotherhood/sisterhood among the students. The MSA will also promote a sense of appreciation of the core Islamic teachings to both Muslims and non-Muslims through its events and activities while providing services to facilitate a comfortable, safe, and peaceful campus environment." (more on its page) (its page was last updated September 2021) [2] Center for Student Involvement has no verified hours for any day. [4]

The Multicultural Center and the Office of Access, Belonging and Community (ABC)'s page "Faith and Spirituality" says: "Ramapo’s faith-based student organizations provide opportunities to explore faith, connect with others, celebrate traditions, and build community. Whether you’re looking for a community that shares your faith or interested in learning about different religious traditions, these organizations offer ways to connect and get involved. Explore their upcoming programs and opportunities below: Muslim Student Association (MSA) InterVarsity Christian Fellowship (IVCF) Newman Catholic Hillel Chabad Interfaith Prayer & Reflection Space…" (more on its page) [6]

The page does not say which dates this schedule covers. [3][5]

I don't have verified information about that part.

question: whats orgo 1 about n does it have a seperate lab? how many credits is it all together

body.answer:
Organic Chemistry I introduces organic chemistry’s language, theory and structure—including alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, alcohols, carbonyl compounds and stereochemistry—and IR and NMR spectroscopy. It emphasizes synthesis and the properties of organic compounds. [1]

Yes. CHEM 211L Organic Chemistry I Lab is separate; it covers laboratory techniques for identifying, purifying, separating, synthesizing and analyzing organic compounds, with emphasis on organic chemistry techniques and synthesis. [2] CHEM 211 is 4 credits and CHEM 211L is 1 credit, so together they are 5 credits. [1][2] The lab’s catalog description also says, “Course fee required.” [2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM211) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM211L)

Organic Chemistry I introduces organic chemistry’s language, theory and structure—including alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, alcohols, carbonyl compounds and stereochemistry—and IR and NMR spectroscopy. It emphasizes synthesis and the properties of organic compounds. [1]

Yes. CHEM 211L Organic Chemistry I Lab is separate; it covers laboratory techniques for identifying, purifying, separating, synthesizing and analyzing organic compounds, with emphasis on organic chemistry techniques and synthesis. [2] CHEM 211 is 4 credits and CHEM 211L is 1 credit, so together they are 5 credits. [1][2] The lab’s catalog description also says, “Course fee required.” [2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM211) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM211L)

question: prereqs for intermediate accounting? do i need both financial n managerial acct done first

body.answer:
For ACCT 321 Intermediate Accounting I (4 credits), the published prerequisite is ACCT 222 Principles of Managerial Accounting. ACCT 222 requires ACCT 221 Principles of Financial Accounting and CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S; CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S may be taken concurrently with ACCT 222. ACCT 221 has no published prerequisites. So both accounting courses are in the prerequisite sequence, but ACCT 221 is a prerequisite to ACCT 222, which is the listed prerequisite to ACCT 321. [2][3][4]
The Registrar says students are responsible for completing all prerequisites before registering, and should review Web Self Service. answer:
HIST 300 Independent Study: History has no published prerequisites, and HIST 101 and HIST 150 also have none published. The catalog does not state a class-year restriction, so it does not indicate that sophomores must first complete an introductory history course to take HIST 300. [3][4][5]

For HIST 300, the catalog describes limited independent-study enrollment: obtain an Independent Study Registration Form from the Registrar, have the instructor and school dean complete it, and return it to the Registrar’s Office. Consult the current Schedule of Classes for independent-study policies. [3]

The Registrar says to review prerequisites in Web Self Service and complete registration in Experience. [12]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [16]

question: how many credits is the enviromental science major n is an internship required

body.answer:
The Environmental Science BS (Bachelor of Science) catalog publishes no total credit count; its requirements list courses only [1]. Neither ENSC 388 CO-OP/INTERNSHIP ENV SCIENCE nor ENST 331 ENVIRONMENTAL INTERNSHIP is listed among the major requirements, so an internship is not required by the published requirements [1]. Both courses are 4 credits: ENSC 388 [2] and ENST 331 [3].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-ENSC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ENSC388) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ENST331)

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

The current catalog lists Elementary Education BS through the School of Arts, Humanities, and Education [1]. Its program description says Teacher Education and Certification is offered through that school [1].

For elementary certification, Ramapo offers a BS in Elementary Education; its FAQ says students intending to pursue this major must meet the Teacher Education Program requirements [2]. It says a separate primary major is required for secondary education, not elementary education [2]. All bachelor’s degree students must declare a major in sophomore year before completing 64 credits [7], and declaring Elementary Education alone does not admit you to the Teacher Education program [6].

**Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [15]

question: junior comm arts major here n i wanna add a music minor. how many courses is it n do i need to audition or take a placement test for the theory classes

body.answer:
The Music Minor requires MUSI 123 Musicianship I, plus 2 lower-level (100- or 200-level) MUSI courses (8 credits total) and 2 upper-level (300- or 400-level) MUSI courses (8 credits total). That is 5 courses altogether; the catalog does not publish a total credit count for the minor. A Music BA is also offered. [1]

The catalog requirement for MUSI 121 Music Fundamentals is a Musicianship Placement Test with a score of 000-074; it does not state an audition requirement. MUSI 121 is not listed in the Music Minor or Communication Arts BA requirements. [1][2][3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-MN-MUSI) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MUSI121)

answer:
The Music Minor requires MUSI 123 Musicianship I, plus 2 lower-level (100- or 200-level) MUSI courses (8 credits total) and 2 upper-level (300- or 400-level) MUSI courses (8 credits total). That is 5 courses altogether; the catalog does not publish a total credit count for the minor. A Music BA is also offered. [1]

The catalog requirement for MUSI 121 Music Fundamentals is a Musicianship Placement Test with a score of 000-074; it does not state an audition requirement. MUSI 121 is not listed in the Music Minor or Communication Arts BA requirements. [1][2][3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-MN-MUSI) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-COMM) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MUSI121)

question: whats the max credits i can take in spring w/o it being an overload, n do i need permission to go over

body.answer:
For a matriculated undergraduate, the spring maximum without an overload is 18 credits. More than 18 requires requesting that the Registrar raise your credit limit; it incurs additional cost. If your cumulative GPA is under 3.0, you need your academic advisor’s approval before requesting it. More than 20 credits also requires approval from your school Dean. The overload form says an overload is only granted with a 3.0 GPA or above: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [1][4][13]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [30]
- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [30]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: graduating may 2027, whens the deadline to apply for graduation n is that the same thing as signing up for commencement

body.answer:
For Spring 2027, apply for graduation by April 1. Applications received after April 1 will not be listed in the Commencement Program. [3]

No. Applying to graduate is required to graduate; commencement is the ceremony celebrating completion or anticipated completion of your degree. January graduates and June and August graduation candidates are invited to participate. [10]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [31]
- **Commencement**: Email: commencement@ramapo.edu. [31]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/commencement/) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: transferred from bergen cc w my AA, does that cover all my gen eds here? also do my AP credits from hs still count or did they get lost when i transfered

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

Admissions says an A.A. from a New Jersey community college waives General Education Requirements once you submit a final official transcript showing the conferred degree. [12] The catalog says the A.A. is fully transferable as the first two years of a baccalaureate degree; specific credit applicability is determined through transfer evaluation and advisement. [3][8] Review your degree audit and meet with your adviser to check your requirements. [19]

AP credit can be considered for transfer; it has not necessarily been lost. [15][7] To award credit, submit your official AP score report to Admissions. [20] After evaluation, you’ll receive a Transfer Credit Evaluation by email showing which courses were accepted, the credit awarded, and the Ramapo equivalent. [18] Check the Transfer Credit Worksheet, which you receive shortly after acceptance, for the number of credits accepted. [13]

**Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [21]

question: what gpa do u need for magna cum laude n do transfer credits count towards it

body.answer:
I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo’s Finance BS (Bachelor of Science) describes preparation for careers in financial analysis, stock brokerage, money management, real estate analysis, banking, insurance and risk management, and international finance. Its Economics BA (Bachelor of Arts) describes studying how societies organize production, distribution and consumption, with attention to the U.S. economy and its global connections. The published material does not establish which major gets you a better job. [1][2]

The Center for Student Success says to focus on subjects and skills that interest you, talk with faculty in your top-choice majors, and consider that majors alone don’t get you a job: job experience does. It recommends co-op or internship experience before graduation. [3] The Center’s goal is to help students choose the right major; its page links to major-choice tips and “I am ready to declare!” [4] Career Development also recommends connecting with faculty and speaking with a Career Advisor at the Cahill Career Development Center. [14] Ramapo publishes that Handshake has more than 10,000 employers registered and on-campus career fairs host more than 200 companies. [9]

For help choosing, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising). For career advice, contact the Cahill Career Development Center. [4][14]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [26]
- **Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [26]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-FNCE) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BA-ECON) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/admitted-students/outcomes/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [26](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

I can't choose for you, but I can share what the college publishes.

Ramapo’s Finance BS (Bachelor of Science) describes preparation for careers in financial analysis, stock brokerage, money management, real estate analysis, banking, insurance and risk management, and international finance. Its Economics BA (Bachelor of Arts) describes studying how societies organize production, distribution and consumption, with attention to the U.S. economy and its global connections. The published material does not establish which major gets you a better job. [1][2]

The Center for Student Success says to focus on subjects and skills that interest you, talk with faculty in your top-choice majors, and consider that majors alone don’t get you a job: job experience does. It recommends co-op or internship experience before graduation. [3] The Center’s goal is to help students choose the right major; its page links to major-choice tips and “I am ready to declare!” [4] Career Development also recommends connecting with faculty and speaking with a Career Advisor at the Cahill Career Development Center. [14] Ramapo publishes that Handshake has more than 10,000 employers registered and on-campus career fairs host more than 200 companies. [9]

question: staying on campus over thanksgiving break do i have to sign up or get permission to stay in my dorm? i live in the village

body.answer:
You may not have to sign up just to stay in your dorm for Thanksgiving: the college’s guest restrictions say guests are permitted during Thanksgiving Break under normal guest procedures. [7] However, the available information does not verify whether residents themselves may remain in housing over the break or need permission. Contact Housing & Residence Life to confirm.

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/policies-guides-forms/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: How do I book an appointment at the writing center? I'm a commuter and returning adult student so I'd prefer to meet online in the evening if thats possible

body.answer:
Book through [Schedule an Appointment](https://ramapocrw.mywconline.com/). Select the day and time, then choose an online session. You can schedule up to one hour before the requested time. [1] The CRW offers virtual consultations to all Ramapo students. [6]

The available information doesn’t say whether evening appointment times are offered. For current availability, contact the Center for Reading and Writing.

**Center for Reading and Writing**: Phone: (201) 684-7557. Email: crw@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons, Room 420. Outreach Coordinator: LC-424; Developmental Writing Specialist: LC-425; Reading Specialist: LC-423. [33]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/crw/schedules/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/crw/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
Ramapo Bookstore (Normal) hours: Monday to Thursday: 9:00am-5:00pm; Friday: 9:00am-4:00pm; Saturday and Sunday: CLOSED. [3] Ramapo Bookstore (Summer) hours: Monday to Thursday: 10:00am-3:00pm; Friday to Sunday: CLOSED. [3] The page adds: "Summer Store Hours: Mon - Thu: 10 am - 3 pm Fri: CLOSED Sat: CLOSED Sun: CLOSED Starting May 14th we will be switching to our Summer Hours" [3] Ramapo Bookstore is in Student Center, 2nd Floor. [1]

Ramapo Bookstore's page "Normal Store Hours" says: "Mon – Thu: 9am-5pm Fri: 9am – 4pm Sat: CLOSED Sun: CLOSED" [2]

Ramapo Bookstore's page "Bookstore Details" says: "The Bookstore is located on the Second Floor of the Robert A. Scott Student Center." [2]

The page does not say which dates this schedule covers. [3]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/csi/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/bookstore/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/about/campus-hours/)

Ramapo’s FAFSA school code is 009344. [2]
For the 2027–2028 FAFSA, returning students should apply by April 1, and new students no later than May 1. [2]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [28]

question: cant pay all of spring tuition at once. how do i sign up for the payment plan, is there a fee, n where's the bursars office if i wanna go in person

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

For Spring, Ramapo offers a four-month or five-month payment plan. The plans do not charge interest; there is a $60 service fee to join. You must enroll and make your first installment before the semester’s payment deadline. [5]

To enroll, use the “Enroll in Payment Plan” button, select the desired term and plan, then review installment due dates and amounts carefully. Choose YES or NO for automatic payments and click Continue. Select a payment method and click Continue, enter bank account or credit card information and click Continue, read the agreement, check “I Agree,” and wait for processing to finish. If you see a message that the plan was processed successfully, you may exit the form. [6]

The Office of Student Accounts is in D-Wing, First Floor.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [35]

This office can help:
**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [36]

Sources: [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [35](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [36](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

For Spring, Ramapo offers a four-month or five-month payment plan. The plans do not charge interest; there is a $60 service fee to join. You must enroll and make your first installment before the semester’s payment deadline. [5]

To enroll, use the “Enroll in Payment Plan” button, select the desired term and plan, then review installment due dates and amounts carefully. Choose YES or NO for automatic payments and click Continue. Select a payment method and click Continue, enter bank account or credit card information and click Continue, read the agreement, check “I Agree,” and wait for processing to finish. If you see a message that the plan was processed successfully, you may exit the form. [6]

The Office of Student Accounts is in D-Wing, First Floor.

question: where do i pick up packages on campus n what address do i put when i order stuff online

body.answer:
Packages are delivered to the Resident Mailroom in the Lodge at the College Park Apartments. You’ll receive an email notification when your package is checked in. Before visiting, make sure you have that check-in notification; bring your Ramapo ID to pick it up. Mailroom hours may vary, so check the Residence Life mailroom website for current hours. [1][2][3][7]

Address packages to:
Complete First Name and Last Name
Ramapo College MB#XXXX
501 Ramapo Valley Road
Mahwah, NJ 07430-1608
Use your complete first and last name and your assigned campus mailbox number. Do not address packages to 501 or 505 Ramapo Valley Road in Oakland, NJ; use Mahwah, NJ 07430. [1][10]

For Amazon orders, you can also choose one of three campus lockers: “cheys” behind C-Wing by the entrance to the Student Center; “ming” outside Thomases Commons in the Village Apartments; or “gelatin” inside the Trustees Pavilion near the cafeteria entrance. [2]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [36]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/mailroom/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/mailroom/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/mailroom/) [36](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i think i have the flu fever n everything. can i just walk into health services or do i need an appt first? does it cost $$

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Drop-in visits are always welcome; you do not need an appointment first. You can also book by calling 201-684-7536 or using [Save Your Spot](https://www.valleyhealth.com/save-your-spot-ramapo-college-health-services). Health Services is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. in the Fall semester. [4]

Visits are not necessarily free: medical services are billed to your insurance, and VMG collects any copay or deductible your plan has at the time of service. Ramapo Aetna Student Health is accepted. [27]

- **Dean of Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7457. Email: deanofstudents@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [34]
- **Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [34]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/official-announcement-health-services-at-ramapo-college-july-14-2026/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/health/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can i register to vote w my dorm adress or do i have to use my home address? anywhere on campus that helps w voter registration

body.answer:
I don’t have verified information about whether you can use your dorm address or must use your home address. The Civic and Community Engagement Center is the most likely office to help with that. Ramapo’s Vote Everywhere program organizes voter registration initiatives and helps students access resources to become educated voters. [7] The Center hosts civic events including National Voter Registration Day; follow its Instagram page and Archway for upcoming events. [4]

**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [30]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/voting-and-political-engagement/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/andrew-goodman-foundation/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm a veteran using my Post-9/11 GI Bill. what do i need to do to get certified for spring 2027 classes, and who's the school certifying official i should contact?

body.answer:
To use Post-9/11 GI Bill® Chapter 33 benefits, apply online at www.gibill.va.gov. Required documents are your Certificate of Eligibility, a copy of your parent’s DD214, and the Ramapo College Veterans Registration Form. The form must be completed each semester, including summer session: [https://www.ramapo.edu/military/wp-content/uploads/sites/259/2022/09/Veterans-Registration-Form.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/military/wp-content/uploads/sites/259/2022/09/Veterans-Registration-Form.pdf) [4]

For Spring 2027, register through Ramapo College Self Service Registration: visit Experience ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Registration Card, click Open Registration Dashboard, then click Register for Classes. You may register any time after your registration window opens. Registration times are based on earned credits as of September 30, 2026; assigned times do not include currently enrolled credits. [13]

Contact the Military and Veterans Success office’s VA Certifying Official, Gina Toriello, School Certifying Official, about requirements to use your VA benefits. [3][9]

**Military and Veterans Success**: Phone: Coordinator of Military and Veteran Enrollment and Success (201) 684-7516; VA Certifying Official (201) 684-7252. Office: E-211. Coordinator of Military and Veteran Enrollment and Success: E-214A. [34]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/military/veteran-points-of-contact/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/military/veteran-aid-program/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/vet-prog/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

To use Post-9/11 GI Bill® Chapter 33 benefits, apply online at www.gibill.va.gov. question: Is there a lactation room on campus for students? I'm a mom going back to school and need somewhere private between classes.

body.answer:
Title IX's page "Lactation/Pumping Space Available" says: "Breastfeeding students, faculty, and staff may request access to a private space on campus to express breast milk. You may reserve the room by contacting Johnie Burton at ext. 7230 or jburton@ramapo.edu. A small refrigerator reserved for the specific storage of breast milk is available. Any breast milk stored in the refrigerator must be labeled with your name and the date of expressing the breast milk. Any nonconforming products stored in the refrigerator may be disposed of. Those storing milk in the refrigerator assume all responsibility for the safety of the milk and the risk of harm for any reason, including improper storage, refrigeration, and…" (more on its page) [2]

Title IX's page "Classes" says: "Your college cannot make you change your major or degree program because you are pregnant or a parent. They cannot force you to attend an alternate program, like an evening program. If a professor doesn’t want you in class because you’re pregnant, tell a school official ASAP. answer:
Title IX's page "Lactation/Pumping Space Available" says: "Breastfeeding students, faculty, and staff may request access to a private space on campus to express breast milk. You may reserve the room by contacting Johnie Burton at ext. 7230 or jburton@ramapo.edu. A small refrigerator reserved for the specific storage of breast milk is available. Any breast milk stored in the refrigerator must be labeled with your name and the date of expressing the breast milk. Any nonconforming products stored in the refrigerator may be disposed of. Those storing milk in the refrigerator assume all responsibility for the safety of the milk and the risk of harm for any reason, including improper storage, refrigeration, and…" (more on its page) [2]

Title IX's page "Classes" says: "Your college cannot make you change your major or degree program because you are pregnant or a parent. They cannot force you to attend an alternate program, like an evening program. If a professor doesn’t want you in class because you’re pregnant, tell a school official ASAP. You have a right to take whatever course you want if you meet course prerequisites. The school official should monitor the class and make sure the professor does not show bias in grading. Stick with it so you can graduate and reach your goals!" (more on its page) [2] Title IX: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance: kmcgee@ramapo.edu To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination and/or sexual misconduct: titleix@ramapo.edu [1] Title IX is in D-104. [1]

Women's Center & LGBTQ+ Services's page "Pregnant & Parenting Students" says: "Lactation/Pumping Space Available Breastfeeding students, faculty, and staff may request access to a private space on campus to express breast milk. Any breast milk stored in the refrigerator must be labeled with your name and the date of expressing the breast milk. Any nonconforming products stored in the refrigerator may be disposed." (more on its page) [4]

Women's Center & LGBTQ+ Services's page "Lounge" says: "During open hours, Ramapo students, staff, and faculty are welcome to stop by Room C-220 hang out, socialize, study, and/or enjoy a hot beverage in the lounge area, which features comfortable seating for relaxing as well as a coffee maker, refrigerator, and microwave. Our space also includes a We Care Satellite Food Pantry ([https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/we-care-program/food-insecurity-resources/](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/we-care-program/food-insecurity-resources/)) stocked with ready-to-eat items like microwave soups and meals, granola and/or breakfast bars, and protein…" (more on its page) [5] Women's Center & LGBTQ+ Services: What if I have more questions about GIH? Please email the Women’s Center & LGBTQ+ Services at women@ramapo.edu. [3] Women's Center & LGBTQ+ Services is in C-220. [3]

Consultants and Supplemental Instruction Leaders (SIs) annually in the spring and summer for the upcoming academic year. We look for academically and culturally diverse candidates who enjoy helping their peers, and we strive to employ students from a wide variety of majors. Consulting for the CRW is more than a job. It is community service on campus with many challenges and rewards, and with those come some pretty serious responsibilities. Not everyone is cut out for this kind of work, and of those who are capable of meeting the demands, there are some who won’t be comfortable making the sacrifices required. A common misconception about consulting is that it is primarily a matter of correcting others’ papers, especially for sentence-level errors, and that therefore an encyclopedic knowledge of grammar, punctuation, mechanics, etc. is what consultants really need in order to do their jobs well. And that’s just not true. Although it’s important that consultants be accomplished readers and writers, teaching grammar is not part of the job description. The foremost requirements are, in as nearly equal measure as possible, a proven commitment to learning, a passion for good writing, and a deep desire to help others. Since, however, those qualities are difficult to measure, we require the following of applicants: Successful completion of CRWT 102 (or AIID 201, if you placed out of CRWT). Minimum grade point average of 3.3; or strong evidence of exemplary academic improvement after a GPA-crushing crisis. Evidence of ability to work both independently and as part of a close-knit group. Evidence of motivation to help others (not necessarily with reading and/or writing). Availability to attend all-day pre-service training during the week before the fall semester begins. Availability to work at least ten hours per week, and to attend in-service training meetings during the academic year. We ask that you provide the following materials in your application (please note: there is no application form; simply gather and submit the materials below together): A one-page cover letter addressing your claims to the requirements above. An unofficial copy of your current academic transcript. A resume. Completed applications may be electronically submitted to Handshake (https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/handshake-students/), Ramapo’s student employment website, at the Writing & Reading Peer Consultants link. question: how do i stop procrastinating istg i have 3 papers due right after thanksgiving break n havent started any

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Start by making each paper smaller: prewriting can help overcome writer’s block and engage you; try listing, clustering, freewriting, looping, or journalists’ questions, then make an organizational plan and tentative outline. [5]

For today, pick one paper and do a short first work session—write down its prompt, list what you know, and start an outline. A Pomodoro resource suggests 25 minutes of work followed by a 5-minute break; MyTomatoes can time and track progress. [20]

The Center for Reading and Writing offers one-on-one consulting and resources for time management and study habits. If the consultant has to spend most of the 40 minutes trying to encourage you to work enthusiastically, or trying to help you find the materials you need, or coaching you to review assignments or materials that you could have familiarized yourself with before coming, then there won’t be so much time left over in which to do the real work of critical thinking. Make no mistake: we will help you with these things, if that’s what’s necessary, and we don’t mind. But the readier you are to get to work, the farther we can help you get in the time allotted. Also, as is the classroom, the Center is a social learning environment. This means that you need to cooperate not only with your consultant, but also with others in the room. The same expectations that apply to the classroom apply to working in the Center: that is, you agree not to disrupt the environment by speaking or laughing loudly, that you respect others’ privacy and personal space, that you wait your turn if necessary, and that you do as directed by Center staff. The following policies apply to all students who come for help in the Center: Students may not receive assistance with a paper due on the day of the session, with the following exception: you may pursue follow-up work that you and a consultant planned during a previous tutorial. If you are coming for a follow-up session, notify the desk attendant when you check in, and indicate which consultant you’re following up with. Consultants do not proofread or edit papers. However, consultants may assist you in reviewing selected sections of the work, identifying patterns of error, and finding resources that you can use to correct the errors, and perhaps avoid or correct them in the future. Students are not allowed to eat during sessions. It’s only 40 minutes; please eat before or after. Silence and put away your phone during the session. If you are waiting for an important call, then wait before meeting with a consultant. There’s no point in wasting your and the consultant’s time on a session if your attention will not be fully engaged for the full duration. If you just can’t spend 40 minutes without looking at your phone, then you have bigger problems than can be solved in the Center. The session notes that your consultant records are private. We will share them with your instructor if you ask us to (this is generally required for CEC credit), but not otherwise, and under no circumstances will they be shared with your parents or other non-College-affiliated parties. question: im a sophomore n everyone keeps talking abt summer internships already like how do ppl even find those, where do i start

body.answer:
Start by updating your resume and profile on Handshake, and use Handshake to find summer internships: [http://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/](http://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/) [1] Ramapo’s Handshake helps students explore career interests and find internships with alumni, companies, and organizations. [7]

Also attend career panels, workshops, and career fairs; investigate careers and jobs you’re interested in; and connect with professionals through informational interviews and career programs. [1] You can meet with a career advisor, who can assist with your job search and provide resources through Handshake and other job sources. [5]

For hands-on practice before applying, try Forage, a free, self-paced virtual work experience with company job simulations. [8] The Cahill Career Development Center can help you get started.

**Cahill Career Development Center**: Phone: Main Office (201) 684-7444; ASB Office (201) 684-7675. Email: careercenter@ramapo.edu. Main Office: C-209; ASB Office: ASB-513. [24]

question: can u book me a study room in the libary for friday at 2pm

body.answer:
I can't send messages or make changes for you, like registering, dropping a class or making a payment.

I can’t book it for you. Friday is November 20, 2026, and rooms can be booked 2 weeks in advance. Go to [https://libcal.ramapo.edu/](https://libcal.ramapo.edu/) and click “Reserve a Study or Media Room.” Choose a category (or “All Categories”), find a room, and select the green availability boxes for your time. Click “Submit Times,” review the booking details and click “Continue,” then fill out the form and click “Submit my Booking.” You’ll receive an email confirmation with a check-in code. Study rooms are for current Ramapo students; only one reservation per day is allowed per person/group. The booking automatically selects 2 hours. Check in when you arrive; if you don’t check in within 15 minutes of the reservation time, the room will be made available to others. Check out when you leave. [1][2]

**Library**: Phone: (201) 684-7575. Email: circ@ramapo.edu. Location: Peter P. Mercer Learning Commons. [30]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/study-rooms-reservations-and-usage/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/library/study-rooms-reservations-and-usage/) [30](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what should i bring to a friendsgiving thats cheap n easy? also is it too late to apply for study abroad for summer 2027

body.answer:
For an inexpensive, easy Friendsgiving dish, try roasted cauliflower, potato latkes, or croutons [11]. The College pages don’t give prices or preparation times, so I don’t have verified information about which option is cheapest or easiest; the Civic and Community Engagement Center may be able to help.

It isn’t possible to tell from the College’s information whether it’s too late to apply for summer 2027: summer program deadlines vary. Check the Study Abroad deadlines page: [https://ramapo.studioabroad.com/index.cfm?FuseAction=Programs.ViewDeadlines](https://ramapo.studioabroad.com/index.cfm?FuseAction=Programs.ViewDeadlines) [33]. Contact the Roukema Center for International Education for help with your application.

**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [34]

Sources: [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/ccec/we-care-fresh-food-distribution/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/summer/study-abroad/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
